name: DarkSPHERE
notes: external.inspire_experiment is null: INSPIRE was not consulted (its rate budget belongs to the supervised importer).
Collaboration: the conceptual design is authored by the NEWS-G Collaboration with Boulby and other participants; DarkSPHERE has no separate collaboration record.
Not NEWS-G3 (the 140 cm detector at SNOLAB inside experiment:news-g): DarkSPHERE is the proposed larger, Boulby-based next step.

physics_goals.quote: DarkSPHERE is primarily designed to search for nuclear recoils from light dark matter in the 0.05--10 GeV mass range.
physics_goals.value: Search for nuclear recoils from light dark matter in the 0.05-10 GeV mass range

summary.plain: DarkSPHERE is a proposed detector for light dark matter: a hollow copper sphere filled with gas, made from copper grown underground at the Boulby laboratory in England. It builds on the NEWS-G experiments and aims to reach the level where neutrinos become the main background.
summary.technical: Proposed next-generation spherical proportional counter electroformed underground at Boulby, a conceptual design of a 3 m diameter helium-isobutane detector inside a 2.5 m water shield in the Large Experimental Cavern (background below 0.01 dru; SI sensitivity 2e-41 cm^2 at 0.1 GeV and 2e-43 cm^2 at 1 GeV; 0.05-10 GeV mass range; also spin-dependent, MeV DM-electron and super-heavy DM tracks). 2026 talk abstracts describe a high-purity copper electroforming facility being commissioned at Boulby and the preparation of a 30 cm version.
